Clause-②: yes
Clause-② reason: measured on `main` `e6175b5`: `useRecordApprovals` is not on `@object-ui/app-shell`'s entry, but `@object-ui/plugin-detail` exports `DetailView`, and sharing one record fetch may give it a prop (a preloaded record or a populate union). «拿不准 ⇒ 按 yes». The seat's `TIER_DEFAULT` review comes before ready; if nothing published moves, the review says so.
Responsibility: n/a — a measured request-count defect on the record page
Thread-read: none
Serial constraints cleared: no open objectui PR touches `RecordDetailView.tsx`, `useRecordApprovals.ts` or `plugin-detail/src/DetailView.tsx` (PR objectstack-ai/objectui#12685 adds only a test beside `RecordDetailView`). objectui#12673 (this seat) touches the list host and may share the detail bridge's record-path builder; this card does not touch the bridge.

  "summary": "Opening a record now sends one approvals read and one record read. Measured live on a HotCRM lead and on a HotCRM opportunity that has a pending approval request. Approvals: useRecordApprovals moves its read and answer into a module-scoped store keyed by object + record (the same structural choice as sharedUserFeeds.ts, without the polling). Every consumer mounted for a record shares one read; a later mount, such as an authored record:approvals block or a tab opened after load, is served the stored answer; a read already in flight is joined. The entry is dropped when the last consumer unmounts, so re-opening the record reads again. refresh() always reads, and every consumer sees the result. RecordDetailView's invalidation effect now fires only when the nonce actually moves; it used to skip only its first run. Record: record:details passes the new DetailView prop recordFromHost, so the body waits for the page's record and never reads the row itself. PM assumption 1 is FALSIFIED as stated. Caller stacks show all three identical approvals reads came from the ONE useRecordApprovals in RecordDetailView. Two came from its mount effect, which React.StrictMode (on in apps/console main.tsx) replays in development. The third came from the page's skip-the-first-run invalidation effect, which the replay walked through. The fix still covers the real multi-consumer case (an authored page placing record:approvals mounts a second hook instance), and a test pins that case. Assumption 2 is confirmed: the second, narrower crm_lead read comes from record:details' DetailView reading while ctx.data is still null; this one is not a StrictMode effect. Assumption 3 is confirmed: hooks/index.ts exports useRecordApprovals and the app-shell entry's named list does not; the entry is unchanged. The card's assignee was not written.
